explanation: Norwegian ski comes from Old Norse skíð, a split length of wood. English took it up in the 1880s, around the time Fridtjof Nansen crossed Greenland on skis.

claims.text: 'Ski' did not come into English from German, Finnish or Russian.
Norwegian ski comes from Old Norse skíð, a split length of wood.
'Ski' is recorded in English from the 1880s.
Fridtjof Nansen crossed Greenland on skis in 1888.

evidence.restatement: English took ski from Norwegian ski, which comes from Old Norse skid.
English did not borrow ski from German, Finnish or Russian.
Old Norse skid meant a stick or split piece of wood, also a snowshoe.

Dictionaries I know date the English noun ski to the mid-18th century (about 1755, from translations of Scandinavian travel and natural-history writing). The 1880s is when skiing and the word spread widely, not the first record.
